Paper Title: Modeling the Trajectory of Skeletal Muscle Hypertrophy During Resistance Training: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
Paper Summary: This meta-analysis pools 3237 measurements from 480 resistance training studies to model how muscle hypertrophy unfolds over the course of a training program rather than only comparing values from before and after training. The authors find that gains follow a curved pattern with the fastest growth occurring early in a training block and progressively smaller increases as training continues, a pattern that held up when accounting for age, sex, training experience, and how muscle size was measured.
Analytics Title: Netherlands 1-1 (2-3 pens) Morocco Stats: Bounou the Hero in Dramatic Shoot-out Win
Analytics Summary: Opta Analyst's recap of the Netherlands and Morocco round of 32 match applies the company's expected goals model to show that Morocco generated significantly more scoring chance quality across regulation and extra time despite the match ending level. The piece pairs that shot quality breakdown with goalkeeper Yassine Bounou's penalty shootout performance to illustrate how a team can control underlying chance creation yet still need a moment of individual brilliance to advance.

Paper Title: Weekend Cyclists vs. Regular Cyclists: Association of Physical Training Distribution on Performance, Cardiometabolic Parameters and Muscle Oxygen Saturation
Paper Summary: Researchers compared cardiorespiratory fitness, muscle strength, and cardiometabolic markers in 28 amateur cyclists who either concentrated their training on weekends or spread it across three or more days each week. Those who trained only on weekends showed lower fitness and muscle oxygen extraction during exercise along with higher visceral fat and triglycerides, indicating that how training volume is distributed across the week matters in addition to the volume itself.
Analytics Summary: Driveline Baseball's OpenBiomechanics Project, an open dataset of motion capture and force plate data from collegiate pitchers and hitters, shipped a major update adding a Python loader package, runnable example scripts, machine readable data dictionaries, a formal datasheet, and a citation file. The underlying data files were also moved into versioned GitHub releases, making the dataset easier to discover, cite, and use in reproducible sport science analyses.

Paper Title: A Unified Ranking Model for Evaluating Snatch and Clean and Jerk Performances Across Body Mass and Sex
Paper Summary: Researchers analyzed 3412 snatch and clean and jerk performances from International Weightlifting Federation world championships and Olympic events held between 2019 and 2025 to build a statistical model that places lifts from athletes of differing body mass and either sex onto one common performance scale. The model showed that the median performance gap between men and women narrows at lower body masses and that lifters in both disciplines tend to peak in performance around age twenty five, giving other measured or judged individual sports a template for comparing athletes fairly across weight and sex categories.

Paper Title: Technique-Specific Load-Velocity Profiling and Prediction Equation for the Back Squat in Elite Portuguese Rugby Players
Paper Summary: Researchers measured barbell velocity during a paused back squat in twenty five elite rugby players to test whether movement speed at a given load can predict that load as a percentage of one repetition maximum. The resulting model explained about ninety five percent of the variation between velocity and relative load, showing that velocity based tracking can estimate strength loads accurately enough to guide training prescription without frequent maximal testing.
Analytics Title: World Cup 2026 Match Predictor: Day 3, Ensemble and Interactive Analysis
Analytics Summary: A data scientist published a three part build of a public World Cup match predictor in Python, starting with an Elo rating model, adding a Poisson goal scoring model, then combining both into a weighted ensemble with an interactive app. The project walks through the code and reasoning behind each modeling choice, giving a reproducible template for blending rating systems and scoring models to estimate match outcomes.
AI Productivity Title: You're not ambitious enough with Claude
AI Productivity Summary: Christine Zhu describes moving beyond using AI to automate routine busywork toward applying it to high leverage strategic work, sharing specific templates and examples from her own practice. She argues that most people underuse AI tools by asking for small time savings rather than restructuring how they approach ambitious projects, and illustrates the difference with concrete before and after comparisons.

Paper Title: Differences in speed, trunk range of motion, and cycle kinematics between Para-Nordic sit-skiing classes across inclines
Paper Summary: Researchers at NTNU and the Norwegian Olympic Sports Center, including Cecilia Severin, Julia Baumgart, Jan Kocbach, and Gertjan Ettema, measured speed, trunk range of motion, and stroke cycle patterns in Para Nordic sit skiers across different classification groups and terrain inclines. The paper, published online in the Journal of Sports Sciences in the last two weeks, helps clarify how impairment classification and uphill grade jointly shape technique, information that can support more individualized coaching and equipment choices in para Nordic skiing.
Analytics Title: #7 Deep Dive Feature Files: Firmware Updates Week Ending 18 July 2026
Analytics Summary: This firmware digest describes a new automatic FTP, or functional threshold power, detection feature rolling out to the Garmin Venu 4, which estimates a cyclist's threshold power from a paired power meter during a steady or high intensity ride instead of requiring a dedicated test protocol. The post also documents other wearable firmware additions released the same week, offering a concrete look at how consumer devices are folding established performance modeling concepts into automated, on device analytics.
AI Productivity Title: What Did You Do With the Hours AI Saved You This Week?
AI Productivity Summary: A writer describes using the Fable 5 model to move a personal operating system out of a spreadsheet and into a proper database, a task they had helped clients with for years but never completed for themselves. The project grew from one task into several as the writer also improved supporting context files and began exploring search visibility work, showing how quickly extra time gets absorbed by new work instead of becoming leisure.

Paper Title: Effect of an Individualised Swimming and Education Programme on Disability From Chronic Low Back Pain: The EduSwim Randomised Controlled Trial
Paper Summary: Wareham and colleagues randomly assigned seventy six adults with chronic nonspecific low back pain to either eight weeks of an individualised, physiotherapist guided swimming programme paired with telehealth education, or education alone. The swimming group reported roughly thirty percent less disability than the education only group at eight weeks along with much higher treatment satisfaction, and the trial is described as the first randomised evidence that swimming itself, not just general exercise, can meaningfully ease chronic back pain.
Analytics Summary: GoldenCheetah, the long running open source performance analysis platform for cyclists, runners, and triathletes, shipped the first release candidate of version 3.8 with planned activity scheduling tied to training plans, customizable programmable Train View charts, and native Apple Silicon builds. The update also deepens two way sync with the Tredict platform for workouts, body measurements, and heart rate variability, giving individual endurance athletes and coaches another actively developed, freely available option for training analysis.
AI Productivity Title: Computer and Browser Use in Codex: Five Real Examples
AI Productivity Summary: On her How I AI show, product leader Claire Vo walks through five specific ways she now hands routine digital tasks to Codex's computer and browser use feature, including quality checking her own app, running persona based user research, clearing out her LinkedIn inbox, and completing an online purchase. She frames this as a distinct emerging habit from typical chat based AI use, since the assistant operates a browser or computer on her behalf rather than only answering questions in a conversation window.

Paper Title: Effects of passive blood flow restriction on muscle function following exercise-induced muscle damage in recreationally active males
Paper Summary: Mason Howard and colleagues tested whether applying blood flow restriction without any accompanying exercise speeds recovery of muscle strength and soreness after deliberately induced muscle damage in recreationally active men. Published online in the Journal of Sports Sciences in early August 2026, the study suggests passive blood flow restriction could serve as a low effort recovery tool, offering a training load management option that individual sport coaches could test with athletes managing high volume schedules.
Analytics Title: COROS August 2026 Feature Update: Bedtime Consistency and Sleep Stress Metrics
Analytics Summary: Coros rolled out an August 2026 feature update that adds bedtime consistency tracking with a suggested target bedtime and a new sleep stress metric capturing physical and mental strain carried into sleep from hard training, alcohol, or late meals. The update also folds naps into the overall sleep score and lets athletes edit, crop, or merge recorded sleep sessions, giving coaches and athletes a more complete, self service view of recovery straight from a released wearable feature rather than a one off study.
AI Productivity Title: I Stopped Opening Substack. Now I Run the Whole Thing From Claude (or ChatGPT).
AI Productivity Summary: A newsletter writer describes replacing manual Substack publishing with a workflow where Claude or ChatGPT connects directly to the platform through the SubflowAI MCP server, letting the assistant draft, schedule, and manage posts from within the chat interface itself. The account frames this as a concrete shift from opening Substack's own dashboard to running the entire publishing operation through an AI agent, illustrating how connecting an assistant directly to a tool through MCP can remove a repetitive manual step entirely.

Paper Title: Modelling Athletic Ageing Relative to an Estimated Performance Envelope
Paper Summary: Statistician Dae Jin Lee introduced a new modeling framework called RACE that measures how close an individual athlete sits to an age based ceiling on attainable performance, rather than only tracking an average career trajectory. Posted to arXiv on August 10, 2026, the sport agnostic method is built for the sparse and irregular performance records typical of individual athlete careers, giving a way to compare peak proximity and decline rates across athletes in any measured or timed sport.
Analytics Title: Amazfit gains FTMS rowing and manual swim rest tracking
Analytics Summary: The technology site the5krunner detailed an August software update that lets eight Amazfit watches connect to indoor rowing machines broadcasting the Bluetooth FTMS standard, including the Concept2 RowErg, and adds a manual rest control for pool swimming that separates rest periods from stroke by stroke swim data. The same update introduces Athlete Defaults on select models, offering another concrete example of a wearable company shipping structured, device level workout data capture rather than a research study or news recap.
AI Productivity Title: How to build an AI Workflow You'll Actually Use
AI Productivity Summary: Researcher and podcaster Lennart Nacke argues that new AI workflows stick best when they attach to a habit a person already has, rather than asking someone to build an entirely new routine from scratch. He illustrates the idea with a concrete example of converting research paper annotations into three reusable pieces, a claim, a limitation, and a possible implication for a current project, while warning that heavy AI use can just as easily manufacture busywork that was not needed in the first place.
